title: Changing the World by Changing the Data

bias_targets.methodology: Conceptually evaluated through a literature review and theoretical discussion on the necessity of data curation and fair representation to prevent models from learning and amplifying gender stereotypes.

Discussed theoretically by analyzing how uncurated data propagates stereotypes and examining how societal context shifts the manifestation of discrimination (e.g., skin tone acting as a proxy for race in the US vs. ethnicity/caste in India).
Conceptually evaluated through theoretical discussions on how uncurated textual corpora reflect and amplify societal inequalities related to social status, class, and caste.
Addressed theoretically as part of the broader argument for deliberate dataset design to prevent language models from inflicting psychological harm on minority groups based on ability.
Conceptually identified as a dimension of social bias that deep learning models absorb and amplify from uncontrolled, non-representative training data.
